titleStmt.title: UniProt: a worldwide hub of protein knowledge
titleStmt.author: The UniProt Consortium

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: UniProt: a worldwide hub of protein knowledge

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the UniProt Knowledgebase itself - 120 million protein records, of which just over half a million carry annotations a human curator read out of the literature
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: how to keep a knowledge base current, provenance-tracked and correct while the sequence data entering it grows exponentially
span.quote: Our challenge is to capture the growing depth and breadth of information and make it easily available and interpretable to our users.

span.label: a two-year update: expanded reference proteomes especially for viruses, new rule-based and association-rule annotation systems, a bibliography layer built from other databases and text mining, and a licence change to CC-BY 4.0
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: method
span.quote: UniProt has developed two complementary rule-based prediction systems, UniRule and the Statistical Automatic Annotation System (SAAS) to automatically annotate UniProtKB/TrEMBL in an efficient and scalable manner with a high degree of accuracy.

span.label: the gap between what has been sequenced and what has been read - 120 million entries against half a million with curated annotation, and expert curation reaching 35-50% of the curatable literature
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: expert biocuration into Swiss-Prot, rule-based automatic annotation into TrEMBL, redundancy removal into an archive rather than deletion, and evidence tags on every claim from either route
span.term: expert biocuration into Swiss-Prot, rule-based automatic annotation into TrEMBL, redundancy removal into an archive rather than deletion, and evidence tags on every claim from either route
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB) combines reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries, to which data have been added by our expert biocuration team, with the unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries which are annotated by automated systems including our rule-based systems.

span.label: why one wrong curated record matters far beyond itself: functional data is computationally transferred from Swiss-Prot to sequence-related but less studied proteins in TrEMBL, so a correction upstream stops misleading data being added to orthologues on the strength of an over-predictive signature
span.quote: The correct annotation on the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entry will ensure that misleading data is not computationally added to orthologous proteins in UniProtKB/TrEMBL on the basis of an over-predictive protein signature, again highlighting the importance of expert biocuration.

span.label: the growth problem is not more biology but more of the same: 90% of proteins have over 90% identity because sequencing is driven by very similar strains of the same species
span.quote: The continuing growth of sequenced genomes is a challenge for databases as much of this growth is being driven by sequencing of very similar and almost identical strains (90% of proteins have >90% identity) of the same species.

span.label: the premise of the DAAC predictor - that function depends not only on WHICH domains a protein has but on their arrangement and order, so two proteins with the same domain set can do different things
span.quote: UniProt has developed two complementary rule-based prediction systems, UniRule and the Statistical Automatic Annotation System (SAAS) to automatically annotate UniProtKB/TrEMBL in an efficient and scalable manner with a high degree of accuracy.

span.label: how a cluster-level GO term is earned: it is assigned only when every annotated member carries it, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one term from each - agreement across the cluster rather than a majority
span.quote: A GO term is assigned to a cluster when it is found in every UniProtKB member that has GO annotation in this cluster, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one GO term from each such member.

span.label: expert biocuration reaches only 35-45% of the curatable literature for a species, 50% for humans - the coverage gap is measured and published rather than left implicit
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: curation is labour intensive and the authors defend it anyway as the most efficient way to get everything out of a paper - which is a statement about what automation has NOT replaced
span.quote: Expert curation is labour intensive, with curators assimilating and evaluating multiple lines of evidence from the text and figures of relevant publications, but this has repeatedly proven to be the most efficient method of extracting all relevant data from a paper.

span.label: keeping a record current is hard because knowledge of protein function evolves and new techniques produce results that may appear to contradict earlier observations
span.quote: This task can be difficult, as our knowledge of protein function continues to evolve and finer grained experimental techniques provide new knowledge that may appear to contradict previous observations.

span.label: MECHANISMS TO IDENTIFY AND HIGHLIGHT CONTRADICTORY INFORMATION IN EXISTING ENTRIES ARE A FUTURE PLAN, NOT A CAPABILITY - a 120-million-record knowledge base with per-claim evidence still cannot systematically surface where its own entries disagree
span.quote: Future plans for the manual curation activities in UniProtKB include the development of mechanisms to identify and highlight contradictory information in existing protein entries in order to improve rigor and reproducibility.

span.label: redundancy removal is not applied to viruses at all, because their small genomes carry too many variants - a stated exemption with a stated reason
span.quote: Note that redundancy removal procedures are not currently applied to viruses, due to the challenges posed by the high number of variants in the small genomes of these species.

span.label: UPCLASS, the classifier applied to 32 million accession-PMID pairs, has a published recall of 0.62 - so roughly a third of the classifications it should make, it does not
span.quote: UPCLASS has been trained and evaluated with the curated literature and categories in UniProt entries (with precision, recall and F-score of 0.80, 0.62 and 0.70, respectively

span.label: the categorisation of computationally mapped bibliography by source database is described by the authors as not optimal for all literature, which is why the classifier was brought in
span.quote: In the entry publication section, publications providing evidence for a specific annotation type are organized across different categories, such as function, interaction and expression, based on the type of data they contain. This categorization facilitates navigation through the protein entry literature by offering users quick access to literature of interest related to a given protein-topic.

span.label: an evidence tag on every individual piece of captured knowledge, naming its source
span.note: eliminates: a claim in the database being untraceable to where it came from - and it is not restricted to the curated half: automatic annotations carry which system produced them · outcome: held
span.quote: Every piece of knowledge we capture is associated with evidences (see https://www.uniprot.org/help/evidences for further details) to indicate the source of information

span.label: a CAUTION comment recording that a previously reported activity is an unsafe observation, kept on the entry alongside the annotation
span.note: eliminates: a superseded finding either persisting silently or disappearing without trace - the reader gets the claim, the doubt and the reason together · outcome: held
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: redundancy removal that moves ~38% of complete proteomes out of UniProtKB and into UniParc, which retains historical obsolete sequence
span.note: eliminates: growth in near-identical strains swamping the knowledgebase - WITHOUT losing the sequences, which is the difference between a withdrawal and a deletion · outcome: held
span.quote: Most critically, a redundancy removal process was first introduced in 2015. This process identifies and removes almost identical proteomes of the same species before their inclusion in UniProtKB ( https://www.uniprot.org/help/proteome\_redundancy) and places their sequences in UniParc.

span.label: assigning a GO term to a UniRef cluster only when EVERY annotated member has it, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one term from each
span.note: eliminates: a single member's annotation propagating to a whole cluster - the rule requires unanimity or a shared ancestor, not a majority · outcome: held
span.quote: A GO term is assigned to a cluster when it is found in every UniProtKB member that has GO annotation in this cluster, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one GO term from each such member.

span.label: publishing UPCLASS's precision, recall and F-score before applying it at scale
span.note: eliminates: the classifier's error rate being invisible to users of the 32 million pairs it classified - PARTIAL, because knowing recall is 0.62 does not tell a user WHICH third is missing · outcome: partial
span.quote: UPCLASS has been trained and evaluated with the curated literature and categories in UniProt entries (with precision, recall and F-score of 0.80, 0.62 and 0.70, respectively

span.label: prioritising for curation exactly what computational prediction gets WRONG - proteins a signature would place in an enzyme family but which are non-functional through the loss of specific residues
span.note: eliminates: human effort being spent where the automatic systems already succeed, and leaves the curators on the cases where a prediction would be confidently wrong · outcome: held
span.quote: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries serve as a source of functional data for the development and enhancement of bioinformatics prediction tools, so we prioritize the capture of functional data that cannot currently be correctly predicted by computational methods, such as proteins which predictive protein signatures would describe as being part of an enzyme family but are in fact non-functional due to the loss of specific amino acid residues.

span.label: admitting metagenome-assembled genomes only when they show high completeness and low contamination, and removing segmented viruses missing one or more segments
span.note: eliminates: partial or contaminated assemblies entering the knowledgebase as if they were whole proteomes · outcome: held
span.quote: We will include only those MAGs that show a high level of completeness and a low level of contamination.

span.label: re-importing curated data from the domain-specific resources it was contributed to - IMEx, the Complex Portal, GO - rather than duplicating their maintenance
span.note: eliminates: the same fact diverging between UniProt and the specialist database that owns it; each is stored and maintained where it belongs and flows back · outcome: held
span.quote: This example also illustrates the collaborative nature of the UniProt Consortium in that the molecular interactions involved have also been added to the IMEx Consortium ( www.imexconsortium.org) dataset by UniProt curators ( 23), the protein complexes involved curated into the Complex Portal ( https://www.ebi.ac.uk/complexportal/) ( 24) and both the proteins and complexes have been further annotated using GO

span.label: UniProtKB
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB) combines reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries, to which data have been added by our expert biocuration team, with the unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries which are annotated by automated systems including our rule-based systems.

span.label: annotations
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: evidences
span.quote: Every piece of knowledge we capture is associated with evidences (see https://www.uniprot.org/help/evidences for further details) to indicate the source of information

span.label: expert biocuration
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: CAUTION
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: UniParc
span.quote: Most critically, a redundancy removal process was first introduced in 2015. This process identifies and removes almost identical proteomes of the same species before their inclusion in UniProtKB ( https://www.uniprot.org/help/proteome\_redundancy) and places their sequences in UniParc.

span.label: redundancy removal
span.quote: Note that redundancy removal procedures are not currently applied to viruses, due to the challenges posed by the high number of variants in the small genomes of these species.

span.label: InterPro
span.quote: InterPro is used to classify sequences at superfamily, family and subfamily levels and to predict the occurrence of functional domains and important sites. InterPro integrates predictive models of protein function, so-called ‘signatures’, from a number of member databases.

span.label: GO annotation
span.quote: A GO term is assigned to a cluster when it is found in every UniProtKB member that has GO annotation in this cluster, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one GO term from each such member.

span.label: UPCLASS
span.quote: UPCLASS has been trained and evaluated with the curated literature and categories in UniProt entries (with precision, recall and F-score of 0.80, 0.62 and 0.70, respectively

span.label: UniFire
span.quote: UniFire (the UNIprot Functional annotation Inference Rule Engine) is a standalone tool to apply the UniProt annotation rules on third party data. This engine is based on a Business Rules Management System (BRMS) named Drools and is developed in conjunction with an exchangeable format for UniProt rules and the protein data to be annotated.

span.label: curatable literature
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: METTL14
span.quote: Subsequent structural studies have now shown that that only one protein, METTL3, constitutes the catalytic subunit ( 20–22). The other subunit, METTL14, has a degenerate active site that is unable to accommodate donor and acceptor substrates and plays a non-catalytic role in maintaining complex integrity and substrate RNA binding

span.label: METTL3
span.quote: Subsequent structural studies have now shown that that only one protein, METTL3, constitutes the catalytic subunit ( 20–22). The other subunit, METTL14, has a degenerate active site that is unable to accommodate donor and acceptor substrates and plays a non-catalytic role in maintaining complex integrity and substrate RNA binding

span.label: MAGs
span.quote: We will include only those MAGs that show a high level of completeness and a low level of contamination.

span.label: CAUTION → METTL14
span.note: A RECORD HOLDING A CLAIM AND A DOUBT ABOUT THAT CLAIM AT ONCE. The entry keeps the reported methyltransferase activity AND a comment saying the report is an unsafe observation. There is no edge type for `this annotation is flagged as unreliable` - all eight assert that a relation holds, and the whole content of a CAUTION is that something asserted elsewhere should not be relied on. This is CLAUDE_B's quine1951 finding with a WORKING IMPLEMENTATION on the other side: UniProt can write it and we cannot
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: expert biocuration → curatable literature
span.note: A COVERAGE RATIO, WHICH IS A RELATION BETWEEN AN ACTIVITY AND WHAT IT HAS NOT REACHED. Curation captures 35-45% of the curatable literature per species, 50% for humans. `part-of` is wrong, `causes` is wrong, and there is no type for `X covers this fraction of Y` - which is the single most useful thing a knowledge base can say about itself and the thing our own corpus has never stated about its own coverage
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: reviewed versus unreviewed - NOT A QUALITY GRADE BUT A PROVENANCE CLASS, and the two are wildly different sizes. `Reviewed` means a curator assimilated multiple lines of evidence from a paper's text and figures; `unreviewed` means a rule fired. Half a million against 120 million. A user filtering to `reviewed` is not filtering out errors, they are filtering to the fraction a person has read
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB) combines reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries, to which data have been added by our expert biocuration team, with the unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries which are annotated by automated systems including our rule-based systems.

span.label: evidence, in UniProt - A SOURCE TAG ON EVERY INDIVIDUAL CLAIM, not a citation on the record. Each piece of knowledge carries where it came from, and automatic annotations carry which system produced them. This is the same commitment this corpus makes with its `evidence` field, made by a database three orders of magnitude larger
span.quote: Every piece of knowledge we capture is associated with evidences (see https://www.uniprot.org/help/evidences for further details) to indicate the source of information

span.label: CAUTION - A COMMENT TYPE THAT SAYS A PUBLISHED FINDING IS UNSAFE. When structural work showed METTL14 has a degenerate active site, the earlier reported methyltransferase activity was not deleted and not silently overwritten: a CAUTION comment was added to tell users the initial report is `an unsafe observation`. THE RECORD CARRIES BOTH THE CLAIM AND THE DOUBT
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: removed, of a proteome - MOVED TO AN ARCHIVE, NOT DELETED. Redundancy removal has taken about 38% of complete proteomes out of UniProtKB and placed their sequences in UniParc, which holds a complete set of known sequences including historical obsolete ones. A withdrawal convention at the scale of 241 million proteins
span.quote: Most critically, a redundancy removal process was first introduced in 2015. This process identifies and removes almost identical proteomes of the same species before their inclusion in UniProtKB ( https://www.uniprot.org/help/proteome\_redundancy) and places their sequences in UniParc.

span.label: prediction precision, of the UniRef GO propagation - MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN EARLIER OUTPUT. The >97% figure comes from comparing sequences that newly acquired a GO annotation with ones the same system annotated in previous releases. That is self-consistency across releases, which is worth knowing and is not external validation against experiment
span.quote: We evaluated the GO term prediction by comparing the protein sequences that newly acquired GO annotation with the ones that GO terms were assigned by UniRef in previous releases. The overall rate of prediction precision is higher than 97%, in all three GO domains, indicating the confidence to propagate UniRef GO annotation to member sequences.

span.label: curatable literature - THE DENOMINATOR THEY MEASURE THEMSELVES AGAINST, and it is not the literature. Coverage of 35-45%, rising to 50% for humans, is a share of the papers judged curatable for a species, so a paper outside that judgement is not counted as missed
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: contradicts → the initial characterisation of METTL14 as a methyltransferase, based on reported activity and MT-A70 family membership
span.note: `contradicts` is right here and it was not for cruz-jentoft2018's mass criterion. The paper does not demote the earlier claim, it reports that structural work showed the active site is degenerate and cannot accommodate the substrates - the earlier finding is not narrowed, it is wrong, and UniProt flags it as unsafe rather than deleting it
span.quote: Subsequent structural studies have now shown that that only one protein, METTL3, constitutes the catalytic subunit ( 20–22). The other subunit, METTL14, has a degenerate active site that is unable to accommodate donor and acceptor substrates and plays a non-catalytic role in maintaining complex integrity and substrate RNA binding

span.label: extends → the UniProt Consortium's own previous database update, published in the same journal in 2017
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: builds-on → InterPro and its member databases PROSITE, SMART and Pfam, whose predictive signatures classify sequences and predict domains for the unreviewed records
span.quote: InterPro is used to classify sequences at superfamily, family and subfamily levels and to predict the occurrence of functional domains and important sites. InterPro integrates predictive models of protein function, so-called ‘signatures’, from a number of member databases.

span.label: predicts → the authors of future papers, who are asked to write protein mentions as (UniProtKB: P68369) so curators and text-mining tools can connect their work
span.note: an instruction to a literature that does not exist yet, and the paper defers to any journal that already has its own format - a standard proposed with its own exception attached
span.quote: We request that authors use the following format (UniProtKB: P68369) to describe a protein within the text of a paper. This formatting follows the compact identifier representation that has been recently proposed to enable uniform resolution of biomedical resource identifiers

span.label: builds-on → the specialist resources this data is contributed to and re-imported from - the IMEx Consortium, the Complex Portal and the Gene Ontology
span.quote: This example also illustrates the collaborative nature of the UniProt Consortium in that the molecular interactions involved have also been added to the IMEx Consortium ( www.imexconsortium.org) dataset by UniProt curators ( 23), the protein complexes involved curated into the Complex Portal ( https://www.ebi.ac.uk/complexportal/) ( 24) and both the proteins and complexes have been further annotated using GO

span.label: annotations —part-of→ UniProtKB
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: evidences —part-of→ annotations
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — RETYPED IN THE AUDIT from `annotations --operationalised-as--> evidences`, where my own note conceded it was not a measurement relation. The quote says every piece of knowledge is ASSOCIATED WITH evidences, which is attachment - and attachment is what `part-of` says
span.quote: Every piece of knowledge we capture is associated with evidences (see https://www.uniprot.org/help/evidences for further details) to indicate the source of information

span.label: CAUTION —part-of→ annotations
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — a comment type carried on an entry beside its annotation - the mechanism by which a record holds a claim and a doubt about that claim at the same time
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: METTL3 —distinct-from→ METTL14
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — and the distinction is the whole point: they are both MT-A70 family members and both were reported to have methyltransferase activity. Only one has a working active site
span.quote: Subsequent structural studies have now shown that that only one protein, METTL3, constitutes the catalytic subunit ( 20–22). The other subunit, METTL14, has a degenerate active site that is unable to accommodate donor and acceptor substrates and plays a non-catalytic role in maintaining complex integrity and substrate RNA binding

span.label: redundancy removal —causes→ UniProtKB
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.9 — and the reduction is the point - the paper reports that it made growth scalable rather than merely smaller
span.quote: Currently this process has removed ∼38% all complete proteomes (∼241 million proteins) from UniProtKB.

span.label: 120 million protein entries, of which just over half a million carry annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase is a collection of sequences and annotations for over 120 million proteins across all branches of life. Detailed annotations extracted from the literature by expert curators have been collected for over half a million of these proteins. These annotations are supplemented by annotations provided by rule based automated systems, and those imported from other resources.

span.label: expert biocuration reaches 35-45% of the curatable literature per species, 50% for humans
span.quote: We have previously demonstrated that UniProtKB expert biocuration captures between 35 and 45% of the curatable literature for any given species, rising to 50% of the curatable literature for _Homo sapiens_

span.label: redundancy removal has taken about 38% of complete proteomes out of UniProtKB and into UniParc, which made growth scalable rather than merely smaller
span.quote: Currently this process has removed ∼38% all complete proteomes (∼241 million proteins) from UniProtKB.

span.label: virus reference proteomes went from 428 - an order of magnitude below the known species count - after a concerted curation effort
span.quote: At the time of our previous publication, the number of virus Reference Proteomes in UniProtKB stood at 428—practically an order of magnitude less than the number of known viral species (which stands at 4405 according to the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses, or ICTV).

span.label: a claim overturned in the database: METTL14 was reported as a methyltransferase and structural work showed its active site is degenerate; the entry now carries a CAUTION
span.quote: Subsequent structural studies have now shown that that only one protein, METTL3, constitutes the catalytic subunit ( 20–22). The other subunit, METTL14, has a degenerate active site that is unable to accommodate donor and acceptor substrates and plays a non-catalytic role in maintaining complex integrity and substrate RNA binding

span.label: the bibliography layer adds 902,956 unique papers over 363,591 entries, and 36,147,401 accession-PMID pairs
span.quote: Altogether these sources add 902 956 unique papers covering 363 591 entries, with a total of 36 147 401 UniProt accession-PubMed identifier (accession/PMID) pairs (Release 2018\_08).

span.label: UniProt data moved to a CC-BY 4.0 licence to make reuse easier - stated in the paper itself
span.quote: We have recently also updated the terms of our license to a CC-BY (4.0) making it easier for UniProt data to be reused by others.

span.label: UniProtKB = reviewed Swiss-Prot entries curated by an expert team, plus unreviewed TrEMBL entries annotated by automated and rule-based systems
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB) combines reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries, to which data have been added by our expert biocuration team, with the unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries which are annotated by automated systems including our rule-based systems.

span.label: evidences = the source tag attached to every individual piece of captured knowledge
span.quote: Every piece of knowledge we capture is associated with evidences (see https://www.uniprot.org/help/evidences for further details) to indicate the source of information

span.label: CAUTION = a comment telling users that an initially reported finding is an unsafe observation
span.quote: we have added a CAUTION comment to the METTL14 entry to both provide some background and inform users that the initially reported methyltransferase activity is an unsafe observation

span.label: UniParc = the archive holding a complete set of known sequences including historical obsolete ones, where redundancy-removed proteomes go
span.quote: Additionally, we provide the UniRef databases that cluster sequence sets at various levels of sequence identity and the UniProt Archive (UniParc) that delivers a complete set of known sequences, including historical obsolete sequence.

span.label: the UniRef cluster-level GO rule: a term is assigned when every annotated member has it, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one term from each
span.quote: A GO term is assigned to a cluster when it is found in every UniProtKB member that has GO annotation in this cluster, or when it is a common ancestor of at least one GO term from each such member.

span.label: UPCLASS precision 0.80, recall 0.62, F-score 0.70 - published before being applied to 32 million accession-PMID pairs
span.quote: UPCLASS has been trained and evaluated with the curated literature and categories in UniProt entries (with precision, recall and F-score of 0.80, 0.62 and 0.70, respectively

span.label: UniRef GO propagation precision above 97% in all three GO domains - measured by comparing newly annotated sequences against the system's own earlier releases
span.quote: We evaluated the GO term prediction by comparing the protein sequences that newly acquired GO annotation with the ones that GO terms were assigned by UniRef in previous releases. The overall rate of prediction precision is higher than 97%, in all three GO domains, indicating the confidence to propagate UniRef GO annotation to member sequences.

span.label: 90% of proteins have over 90% identity to another, which is what makes the growth a redundancy problem rather than a knowledge one
span.quote: The continuing growth of sequenced genomes is a challenge for databases as much of this growth is being driven by sequencing of very similar and almost identical strains (90% of proteins have >90% identity) of the same species.

span.label: the two provenance classes a UniProt annotation can carry: expert curation into Swiss-Prot, and rule-based automatic annotation into TrEMBL
span.quote: The UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB) combines reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries, to which data have been added by our expert biocuration team, with the unreviewed UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries which are annotated by automated systems including our rule-based systems.

span.label: the two rule systems: UniRule and the Statistical Automatic Annotation System
span.quote: UniProt has developed two complementary rule-based prediction systems, UniRule and the Statistical Automatic Annotation System (SAAS) to automatically annotate UniProtKB/TrEMBL in an efficient and scalable manner with a high degree of accuracy.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gky1049.
